name: Logitech TrueForce Linux driver
description: Linux kernel driver and userspace tools for Logitech's direct-drive wheels (RS50, G PRO) and the G923: force feedback, TrueForce haptics, rev lights and wheel settings, with launch tooling for Proton games.
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the software does and which wheels it drives: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to install, how to report problems (tools/setup.sh report) and how to contribute: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing
contribution_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing describes what contributions are wanted (code, hardware testing, USB captures), what an issue must contain, and how the project is checked without a wheel.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing: an issue carries kernel version, distribution and dmesg (tools/setup.sh report prints them); code changes run the Rust workspace tests and the header-only C harnesses, all of which CI runs on every push.
floss_license_justification: GNU General Public License v2.0 only, the kernel's own license: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/COPYING
license_location_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/COPYING at the top level of the repository.
documentation_basics_justification: README sections Getting started, Install, Force feedback in games, Configuring the wheel and Troubleshooting (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#getting-started), plus the wiki.
documentation_interface_justification: The sysfs interface is documented in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/SYSFS_API.md, the launcher and its environment in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/LAUNCH_OPTIONS.md, the wheel protocol in https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/docs/PROTOCOL_SPECIFICATION.md.
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository, wiki and every download (GitHub releases, AUR, COPR, OBS) are served over HTTPS.
english_justification: All documentation, issues and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: Releases and commits every week; 0.41.0 shipped 2026-09-12 with fixes from that week's reports: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
repo_track_justification: Git; every change is a commit with author, date and message.
repo_interim_justification: Every change is pushed to master as it is made; releases are tags on master, there is no separate private development line.
version_unique_justification: Every release is a tag vX.Y.Z and a GitHub release of the same name: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic versioning: major for sysfs API breaks, minor for new wheels or attributes, patch for fixes and docs, as stated at the top of CHANGELOG.md.
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md, one dated section per release, and the same text on each GitHub release: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been reported against this project so far. CHANGELOG.md is where every fix is described, and a security fix would be identified there and in the release with its identifier.
report_process_justification: Issues on GitHub, as the README asks: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues. tools/setup.sh report prints the environment block an issue needs.
report_responses_justification: Bug reports are answered, usually the same day, with a diagnosis or a request for a specific capture; see any recent issue at https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered and either scheduled or explained: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/SECURITY.md: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository (Security tab, Report a vulnerability), with an email address as the fallback.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within a few days. No vulnerability report has been received so far.
build_justification: The kernel module builds with make (or DKMS), the userspace with cargo build; tools/setup.sh does the whole install from a checkout.
build_common_tools_justification: make and Kbuild for the kernel module, cargo for the Rust workspace, DKMS, and the distribution packagers' own tools (makepkg, debhelper, rpmbuild).
build_floss_tools_justification: Only FLOSS tools are needed: GCC or Clang with the kernel's Kbuild, the Rust toolchain, GNU make. The project is packaged for Arch, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE and NixOS from those alone.
test_justification: cargo test --workspace in userspace/logi-wheel (over a thousand tests), plus header-only C harnesses for the force maths under tests/ (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/tests/README.md).
test_invocation_justification: cargo test --workspace; make -C tests/effect-math run and make -C tests/texture-merge run; CI runs all of them on every push (.github/workflows).
test_most_justification: Coverage is not measured yet. The registry, the parsers, the launcher planning and the proxy logic are tested; the hardware-facing paths are not, as they need a wheel.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every push and pull request: kernel builds on two kernel versions, sparse and smatch, the Rust tests and clippy, CodeQL, cargo-audit, the Nix flake: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/actions
test_policy_justification: Stated in the README's Contributing section: changes that add functionality come with tests for it, and CI runs them on every push (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver#contributing).
tests_are_added_justification: Recent commits show it: the marker sanitiser fix added a bash-backed test, the build stamp added unit and integration tests, the installer change added a packaging test (https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/commits/master).
warnings_justification: The kernel module builds under the kernel's -Wall defaults on 5.15, 6.8 and 7.x in CI, with sparse and smatch on top; the Rust workspace builds with clippy -D warnings on every push.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any clippy warning in the Rust workspace, and the kernel module builds warning-free on every kernel CI builds against.
warnings_strict_justification: clippy with all warnings as errors across the workspace; sparse with -D__CHECK_ENDIAN__ and smatch on the C.
know_secure_design_justification: The driver's inputs are an untrusted USB device and untrusted game or Wine processes. The design keeps them apart: every parser is bounds-checked and fuzzed, device access goes through udev-granted permissions rather than root helpers, workflow tokens are read-only by default, releases are signed, and kernel-side lifetimes are reasoned about explicitly (see the 0.41.0 changelog entries on the deferred force-feedback teardown).
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer works on kernel memory-lifetime bugs (use-after-free in deferred callbacks, re-entrancy, lock ordering) and on input validation for network-fed parsers, documented in CHANGELOG.md and docs/; CodeQL's security queries run on the C.
crypto_published_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.
crypto_call_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography of its own; release artifacts are signed with GnuPG by the packaging pipeline, which is outside the software.

delivery_mitm_justification: Every download is HTTPS: GitHub releases and repository, AUR, COPR, OBS. The Arch repository and its packages are GPG-signed and pacman verifies them.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release packages are signed and the signatures are attached to the release; the Arch repository database is signed; the Debian and RPM channels carry their own signing.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known vulnerability is outstanding; cargo-audit runs in CI and Dependabot watches dependencies.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: None reported so far; the policy in SECURITY.md is a fix on master and a release.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no keys or tokens; the signing key and channel credentials live in GitHub Actions secrets.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (C/C++, security queries) on every push and weekly; clippy with warnings as errors on the Rust workspace; sparse and smatch on the kernel module; SonarCloud: https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/actions
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-and-quality queries on the C; cargo-audit against the RustSec advisory database in CI.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open findings: clippy and cargo-audit gate every push, CodeQL alerts are triaged as they appear.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every push and pull request, plus a weekly CodeQL schedule.
dynamic_analysis_justification: cargo-fuzz targets for every parser that reads bytes from a game or a Wine process (the relay datagram, the PID report decoder, and each UDP telemetry decoder): https://github.com/mescon/logitech-trueforce-linux-driver/blob/master/userspace/logi-wheel/fuzz
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The kernel module is exercised under a KASAN, lockdep and kmemleak debug kernel in the development VM whenever lifetime or locking code changes; the 0.40.3 timer race was reproduced and verified there. The Rust side is memory-safe and fuzzed.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz targets run debug builds with Rust assertions enabled; the kernel module keeps its WARN_ON checks in production builds.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis finding is open; the first fuzz run found nothing, and a panic found that way would be fixed before the next release.
